podcast.title: Controversial Licensing and Lawsuits
podcast.body: Abkco Music initially licensed a snippet of "The Last Time" to The Verve for "Bittersweet Symphony" in exchange for 50% of earnings. Subsequently, Abkco sued The Verve, alleging the band used more of the sample than agreed, and ultimately forced them to surrender 100% of the song's publishing rights. Abkco then controversially licensed The Verve's now-owned recording to Nike for a TV commercial. "Abco Music sued saying that the Verve used more of the sample than was spelled out in the licensing agreement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Copyright Acquisition of "Bitter Sweet Symphony"
podcast.body: Abkco, the company that administers the works of The Rolling Stones, gained full copyright to The Verve's song "Bitter Sweet Symphony" after the band lost a legal challenge over excessive sampling from a Stones-related cover. Abkco subsequently licensed the song to Nike for a commercial in 1998, against The Verve's wishes. "Abco sued, got the rights to bittersweet symphony, and immediately licensed it to Nike."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 1

podcast.title: Publishing and Copyright Ownership
podcast.body: Abkco Music held the publishing and copyright for The Rolling Stones' song "The Last Time" and its orchestral rendition by the Andrew Loog Oldham Orchestra. The company was controlled by Allen Klein. "Abco Music, the company that owned the publishing and the copyright to that song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
